note: Five active units: approved foundations and the researched three-chapter data/adaptation/evaluation section. Numbers express current reading order; stable concept IDs survive reordering. No learner sessions conducted.

units.title: How Language Models Work
units.outcome: Explain how training changes a model and how that model generates an answer.
units.activity: Trace one answer through tokenisation and generation, then propose changes for new Sunday hours, brief answers and live catalogue availability. Explain where information goes, whether parameters change, required materials and a test. Add one material needed to investigate original training.
units.criteria: Explain the generation loop and fixed weights during ordinary inference. Distinguish request context, retrieval, training and tool execution; connect each intervention to necessary materials and an appropriate test. Explain a researcher’s additional need.
outcomes: Explain how training changes a model and how that model generates an answer.
Trace how prompts, retrieved documents and tools contribute to an application.
Identify the components and release materials needed to run, adapt or investigate a model.

units.title: What ‘Open’ Means
units.outcome: Distinguish a model release from a hosted application or model service.
units.activity: Assess Cedar and Rowan against the library’s adaptation and sharing requirements. Recommend a deployment route, cite the supplied terms, identify an unresolved practical question and a revision condition.
units.criteria: Trace who operates the model; cite permissions and restrictions; distinguish absent from uninspected information; explain practical fit and a feasible next check.
outcomes: Distinguish a model release from a hosted application or model service.
Assess release materials and terms, including open weights and open-source AI.
Recommend a release and deployment route for a purpose, with unresolved checks.

units.title: Where Model Data Comes From
units.outcome: Distinguish data used in context, training and evaluation.
units.activity: Create a record-by-record data-use plan, a split rule and a coverage check.
units.criteria: Distinguish context/training/test roles, provenance, permission and related families; do not infer performance from an inventory.
outcomes: Distinguish data used in context, training and evaluation.
Explain how selection and provenance affect a dataset’s use.
Design a data split and identify missing coverage.

units.title: How Models Are Adapted
units.outcome: Choose an intervention at the context, application or parameter level.
units.activity: Annotate a teacher–student pipeline and design a controlled comparison.
units.criteria: Locate weight changes, keep non-training changes visible and address confounders and regressions.
outcomes: Choose an intervention at the context, application or parameter level.
Trace demonstrations, preferences and teacher–student signals.
Design a comparison that addresses alternative explanations.

units.title: How to Judge a Model
units.outcome: Specify evaluation conditions and score outputs under a rule.
units.activity: Write a 250–400 word decision note using the fictional task comparison.
units.criteria: Reproduce both means, justify priorities, explain limited evidence and represent an alternative next step.
outcomes: Specify evaluation conditions and score outputs under a rule.
Calculate and interpret a task-weighted comparison.
Recommend a next step with counterarguments and uncertainty.
